observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a wide triangular mass of overlapping grey-violet carapace plates that rise to a pointed crested head plate in the centre. Under it hangs a cluster of ivory fangs/mandibles, and a fringe of pale spike-legs runs along the bottom edge. East: a long segmented body in profile, low and thin at the tail (left) and rising to a tall, spiny, armoured head (right) with fangs hanging down. Each segment has a pale claw-leg. North: a narrow, elongated oval spine of chevron-stacked plates, wider at the top and tapering to a point at the bottom, edged on both sides by pale claw-legs. No eyes or face anywhere on north. All three share one palette and plate texture.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. A head-on armoured head with a central keel crest and a frame of layered plates. A ring of curved ivory fangs forms a mouth, with a dark ribbed throat visible below the fangs. Flanking segments fan out wide to either side like a pyramid, and spike-legs line the bottom. Painterly stone-grey texture with fine pitting. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Side profile. Body segments get progressively taller from the tail to the head, so the silhouette is a ramp. A dorsal row of hooked spines runs along the top. The head is armoured with downward fangs, and there is one claw-leg per segment along the ground line. Clean alpha, no shadow.
observed.north.png: A long, narrow dorsal plate column. Chevron plates point upward, the column narrows to a tail point at the bottom, and claw-legs fringe both sides. No face. It reads mostly as looking down onto the back from above, with little sense of the body receding away from the camera.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature spans about two cells long and roughly 1.3 cells tall, clearly bigger than the human's body. At 32 px/cell it reads as a dark grey spiny segmented slug shape, distinct from the brown ground and bigger than the human and the rat.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head on, facing the camera: crest, fangs and mouth ring centred, flanks fanning back.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back plates and the tail tip at the bottom. No eyes, fangs or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: North is a narrow, symmetric dorsal column with even chevron plates and legs splayed at both edges. It reads as looking straight down on the back, not as the rear seen at the game's angle with the body receding.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 19% spread comes from east being a lower profile ramp (tail low, head high) against the taller south/north views. That is pose and silhouette, not a scale jump. Plate and leg sizes match across facings.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same grey-violet pitted carapace, ivory claw-legs and spined plates on every facing. The head crest and fangs appear on south and east and are correctly hidden on north. South's very wide pyramid flare is broader than north's column, but a long body seen end-on can plausibly read this way.

ALIEN.seen: It is nearest a centipede or isopod, but the armoured fanged head, stone-grey plating and hooked dorsal spines would not be named as an Earth species at a glance. All departures are present.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) Massive: about two cells long and taller than the human in scale.png, so present. 2) Predator head: a fanged, armoured head with a mouth ring on south and east, so present. 3) Alien skin: grey-violet pitted stone-like carapace plates with spines, no pink flesh or clitellum, so present.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art matching the description. Not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: All three facings sit cleanly on the checkerboard with no ground patch, shadow or halo.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a dark spiny segmented creature with a raised head, distinct from the ground.
